title: Kedgeree
subtitle: Smoked haddock and rice with boiled eggs and curry spices
excerpt: A British breakfast and brunch classic of flaked smoked haddock, basmati rice, boiled eggs, butter, and curry spices. Gentle and warming, satisfying at any time of day.

recipe.sourceNotes: Kedgeree is a British dish descended from the Indian khichri (rice and lentils cooked together with spices), which was adapted by British colonists in India and brought back to Britain where it evolved into its modern form using smoked fish, boiled eggs, and curry powder. The dish became a staple of the Victorian and Edwardian breakfast table, where it was typically served at the sideboard as part of the hot breakfast. The smoked fish and gentle curry spice are the defining flavour combination. Smoked haddock (undyed) is traditional; a combination of smoked haddock and smoked salmon is popular in modern versions. The eggs are hard-boiled and quartered or soft-boiled and halved depending on preference. Kedgeree is now eaten at any meal and has become firmly established in the British repertoire as a comfort dish.

recipeTools.notes: A large saucepan for the haddock and a wide saucepan or deep frying pan for the rice.

content.text: Poach the smoked haddock in milk rather than water: the milk tempers the smokiness and produces a creamier, more rounded flavour. The poaching milk can be used as part of the cooking liquid for the rice or discarded. Remove the haddock from the milk as soon as it flakes easily: overcooked smoked haddock becomes dry and stringy. Flake it into large pieces rather than small fragments; the texture is better and the pieces remain distinct in the finished dish.

Put the smoked haddock in a wide pan skin-side down. Pour over the milk and add the bay leaves. Bring to a simmer and poach for 8 to 10 minutes until the fish flakes easily. Lift out the fish and leave to cool. Remove the skin and flake into large pieces. Strain and reserve the milk.

Melt the butter in a large, wide pan over medium heat. Fry the onion for 8 minutes until soft. Add the curry powder and turmeric. Cook for 1 minute. Add the rice and stir to coat. Pour in enough water to cook the rice according to packet instructions (about 600 ml). Season. Bring to the boil, cover, and cook on low heat for 12 minutes until the rice is tender.

Fold the flaked haddock into the rice very gently, taking care not to break up the flakes. Add the lemon juice. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Scatter with parsley and add the boiled egg quarters. Serve immediately.
